rules.name: sync-requires-authorization-filter-main
rules.reason: Decision 2 (spec-v6-bdc-readiness.md), main consent contract only: with HPDS_REQUIRE_AUTHORIZATION_FILTER on (Java's hpds.requireAuthorizationFilter, on by default and on at BDC), Rust refuses /query/sync with 400 when authorizationFilters is missing, null or empty, or becomes empty because a repeated key keeps its last value []. Java main runs no validator on sync and answers over every patient (QueryV3Service runs QueryValidator only on POST /query). INFO_COLUMN_LISTING is exempt, as the harmonization contract exempts it from the consent requirement, since it reads no patient data. BDC's query service always sends \_consents\ on the auth backend, so no BDC answer changes. Accepted only on sync, only when the comparison says the flag is on (--require-authorization-filter, on by default), only for a query with no authorization filter, and only with Rust's 400 holding exactly main mode's message 'Authorization filter is required for this query: authorizationFilters is missing or empty and hpds.requireAuthorizationFilter is on', against Java's 200 with a body, or against Java failing on another part of the query (a 200 with an empty body, or a 500), a part Rust's earlier refusal never reaches.

rules.name: unknown-field-main
rules.reason: Decision 6 (spec-v6-bdc-readiness.md), main consent contract only: main mode knows the seven fields of main's Query (select, authorizationFilters, phenotypicClause, genomicFilters, expectedResultType, picsureId, id). An unknown field anywhere, userConsents included, or a clause mixing filter and subquery fields, makes Java's default ObjectMapper throw in convertIncomingQuery, which PicSureV3Service answers with 500 on /query/sync and POST /query. Rust answers 400 naming the field. Accepted only when the request holds a field that Query, AuthorizationFilter, PhenotypicFilter, PhenotypicSubquery or GenomicFilter does not declare, with Rust's 400 holding "unknown field `<name>`" for one such field against Java's 500.

rules.name: null-authorization-filter-main-status
rules.reason: Decision 2 (spec-v6-bdc-readiness.md), main consent contract only: a null element of authorizationFilters, a null or missing conceptPath, null or missing values, or a null value looked up in a categorical concept makes Java main throw while evaluating (a NullPointerException in authorizationFiltersToPhenotypicClause or the cube cache, or IllegalArgumentException 'Either values or one of min/max must be set for a filter'), which AuditLoggingFilter answers 200 with an empty body with audit logging off (BDC's configuration) and 500 with it on. On POST /query a null element or null path throws a NullPointerException in QueryValidator that escapes runQuery: 200 with an empty body (or 500) and no job. Null or empty values there end the job in ERROR, which Rust matches. Rust refuses the sync request and the submit with 400 and exactly one of main mode's messages: 'an authorization filter is null', 'an authorization filter's conceptPath is null', 'an authorization filter's values are null' or 'an authorization filter's values hold null'. Accepted only when the query holds such a null and Rust's message is the one for a kind of null it holds (a null filter, a null or missing path, null or missing values, a null value), with that refusal against Java's empty 200, its 500, or its submit answered 200 or 500 with no status. In main mode it replaces null-authorization-filter-main.

rules.name: genomic-static-refusal-empty-cohort-main
rules.reason: Divergence by design, main consent contract only: Rust keeps v5's refusals of a genomic filter that is invalid as sent (a null filter, key, zygosity or categorical value, a spec key whose position Java cannot read, a numeric filter with one bound or with min above max), decided from the request alone. Java main skips the genomic step when the phenotype cohort is empty, which in main mode includes every query whose authorization filters select nobody, and answers as over no patients. Accepted only when Rust's 400 is exactly one of the refusals the request's genomic filters draw, and Java's answer is the answer over no patients or no variants (a count of 0, cross counts of 0, an empty list, No Variants Found, an export with no rows).

rules.name: invalid-request-status
rules.reason: Spec divergence, HTTP errors: Java answers a bad sync query or a validation failure with 500 (the query service then returns 502); Rust returns 400 with a text message. When the comparison knows which side is Java, the 500 must be Java's: a Rust 500 against a Java 400 is a Rust failure and stays flagged.

rules.name: unknown-async-id-status
rules.reason: Spec divergence, HTTP errors: Java answers an unknown async result id with a NullPointerException 500; Rust returns 404.

rules.name: invalid-request-empty-200
rules.reason: Spec divergence, HTTP errors: Java answers a FILTER with neither values nor a range, or an empty subquery, with 200 and an empty body; Rust returns 400 with a text message. The rule covers only these entries and only when the 200 side's body is empty. Genomic filters sent to an HPDS without genomic data are genomic-no-store-refused.

rules.name: unknown-async-id-status-empty-200
rules.reason: Spec divergence, HTTP errors: Java answers /status for an unknown async id with 200 and an empty body; Rust returns 404.

rules.name: observation-cross-count-defect
rules.reason: Java OBSERVATION_CROSS_COUNT defect: with two or more selects it can drop keys, write -1 for a key whose concurrent TreeMap.put threw, or hang. Accepted when one side's key set is a strict subset of the other's and every shared key matches, when, with the Java side known, Java's keys are all in Rust's with every value equal or -1 and at least one -1 (only Java writes -1), or when a side times out.

rules.name: search-max-double-min-value
rules.reason: Spec divergence, LowRAMLoadingStore.complete and LoadingStore initialize max to Double.MIN_VALUE, so a numeric concept with no value above zero reports a max of 4.9E-324; /search returns that stored max, where Rust returns the real one. Accepted only when every other field of the search body is equal and the real max is zero or below.

rules.name: range-min-above-every-value-empty-200
rules.reason: Spec divergence, Range filters: Java's seekForMinIndex throws when min is above every value (on the harmonization branch, every value of any one selected partition holding the concept), and copyOfRange throws when max is below min; Java then answers 200 with an empty body, where Rust answers 200 with the result for an empty cohort. Accepted only for sync entries whose phenotypic clause holds a FILTER with a min, and only when the empty 200 body is Java's (the run must name its Java side with --java and --java-branch) and Rust's 200 has a body. A string min counts when Jackson coerces it to a number ("NaN" is above every value), and an entry sent as a raw body is read from that body.

rules.name: missing-consents-sync-empty-200
rules.reason: Decision 7 (plan-v2.md) and README, Differences from Java: 'With HPDS_REQUIRE_AUTHORIZATION_FILTER true, a query with no consent value is a 400 "User consents are required for this query" on both query routes. Java answers /query/sync 200 with an empty body and no queryMetadata header'. Accepted only when the entry's query carries no userConsents value, the 400 body is exactly that message (which Rust sends only with the flag on), and the 200 side's body is empty. A 400 for any other reason, such as values on a numeric concept on an unpartitioned store, does not match.

rules.name: missing-consents-async-error
rules.reason: Decision 7 (plan-v2.md) and README, Differences from Java: with the flag on and no consent value Rust refuses POST /query with 400 "User consents are required for this query", where Java answers 'POST /query 200 with a status of ERROR'. Accepted only when the entry's query carries no userConsents value and the refused submit's body is exactly that message, so a sync type submitted on the async route or any other refusal does not match.

rules.name: search-category-values-order
rules.reason: Decision 9 (plan-v2.md) and README, Differences from Java: '/search writes concepts in path order and categoryValues sorted. Java's order of both is unspecified'. Accepted only when sorting every categoryValues array makes the bodies equal.

rules.name: search-concept-order
rules.reason: README, Differences from Java: '/search writes concepts in path order ... Java's order of both is unspecified (an immutable map whose order changes with every start, a HashMap, a HashSet)'. Applies to the null-term answer, an array of one-entry objects. Accepted only when sorting those arrays by path makes the bodies equal.

rules.name: search-concept-and-category-values-order
rules.reason: README, Differences from Java: '/search writes concepts in path order and categoryValues sorted. Java's order of both is unspecified'. For the null-term answer both orders differ at once. Accepted only when sorting the concept array by path and every categoryValues array makes the bodies equal.

rules.name: search-order-and-double-min-value
rules.reason: README, Differences from Java ('/search writes concepts in path order and categoryValues sorted') together with the Spec divergence that LoadingStore starts max at Double.MIN_VALUE, which CSVLoader also uses per partition (harmonization-delta.md section 1, 'The Double.MIN_VALUE max quirk ... apply per partition'). Accepted only when the three normalizations together make the bodies equal.

rules.name: dataframe-tie-order-across-partitions
rules.reason: Decision 4 (plan-v2.md): 'Exports and per-value cross counts merge per-partition by_key data with a k-way merge on patient, with a fixed tie order (partition name order). Java's order across partitions is unspecified, so the order is whitelisted.' A patient in several partitions gets the same values in a cell in another order. Accepted only when sorting the tab-separated values inside every cell makes the exports equal.

rules.name: range-min-above-partition-values-async-error
rules.reason: Spec divergence, Range filters ('Java's seekForMinIndex throws when min is above every value'), which on the harmonization branch applies per partition: a min above every value of one selected partition holding the concept throws, so the Java async query ends in ERROR where Rust answers the cohort. Accepted only for entries whose phenotypic clause holds a FILTER with a min, and only when the ERROR is Java's (the run must name its Java side with --java and --java-branch) and Rust's query succeeded.

rules.name: duplicate-key-last-wins
rules.reason: README, Differences from Java: 'Request bodies holding the same key twice in any object, the envelope, the query, a clause or a userConsents entry included ... are a 400. Jackson keeps the last copy.' Accepted only for the duplicate-key entries. Under the main consent contract the entry must repeat a key other than authorizationFilters and Rust's refusal must name it: main keeps the last authorizationFilters value as Jackson does (Decision 6), so a refusal of that repetition stays reported.

rules.name: values-on-numeric-status
rules.reason: Java error, invalid input: a FILTER with values on a numeric concept makes PhenoCube.getKeysForValue throw a ClassCastException (PhenoCube.java:54-55), so Java answers /query/sync 200 with an empty body and ends POST /query in ERROR. Rust refuses the query with 400 "<path> is not a categorical variable". Accepted only for that message against Java's empty 200 or async ERROR.

rules.name: filter-shape-status
rules.reason: Spec divergence, HTTP errors: POST /query runs Java's PhenotypicFilterValidator, which throws IllegalArgumentException for a REQUIRED or ANY_RECORD_OF filter with values or a bound, and for a FILTER with both values and a bound; Java catches it and ends the query in ERROR (QueryV3Service.runQuery). Rust refuses the submit with 400 and the validator's own message. Accepted only when the query holds such a filter, Rust's 400 is exactly that filter's message, and the Java side ended in ERROR or answered an empty sync 200.

rules.name: range-on-categorical-status
rules.reason: Java error, invalid input: a FILTER with min or max on a categorical concept casts the cube's values to Double and throws (PhenoCube.java:100-103), so Java answers /query/sync 200 with an empty body and ends POST /query in ERROR. Rust refuses the query with 400 "<path> is not a numeric variable". Accepted only for that message against Java's empty 200 or async ERROR.

rules.name: sync-type-on-async-route
rules.reason: README, Differences from Java: 'POST /query accepts only PATIENTS, DATAFRAME, DATAFRAME_TIMESERIES and DATAFRAME_PFB'. Java accepts a sync result type there and then fails it. COUNT, CATEGORICAL_CROSS_COUNT and CONTINUOUS_CROSS_COUNT are queued and end in ERROR (CountV3Processor.java:211 throws UnsupportedOperationException on the worker). CROSS_COUNT and OBSERVATION_CROSS_COUNT make initializeResult throw RuntimeException("UNSUPPORTED RESULT TYPE") (QueryV3Service.java:122), outside the IllegalArgumentException catch; on both Java images the submit still answers 200 with an empty body and no status (checked against main 7798b1c84 and feature-harmonization ecf5a5315). Rust refuses the submit with 400 "Result type <type> is computed synchronously. Submit it with POST /query/sync.". Accepted only for async entries with that exact message for the entry's result type, against a submit Java accepted with 200.

rules.name: genomic-type-on-async-route
rules.reason: Spec section 1 and the plan-v5.md decision of 2026-10-20 on the oracle: genomic result types and INFO_COLUMN_LISTING on POST /query stay unsupported in Rust, as in Java. Java has no processor for them in initializeResult (QueryV3Service.java:118, the switch default throws RuntimeException outside the IllegalArgumentException catch), so its submit answers 200 with no body or the job ends in ERROR. Rust refuses the submit with 400 "result type <type> is not supported by POST /query; send it to POST /query/sync". Accepted only for async entries with that exact message for the entry's result type, against Java's bodiless 200 or ERROR.

rules.name: request-limit-status
rules.reason: README, the HPDS_MAX_* settings: Rust bounds the shape of every query (HPDS_MAX_SELECT_PATHS 5,000 selects, HPDS_MAX_CLAUSE_DEPTH 64 levels, HPDS_MAX_CLAUSE_NODES 10,000 clauses, HPDS_MAX_QUERY_CONCEPTS 20,000 touched concepts), and its JSON reader refuses bodies nested past serde_json's recursion limit of 128, about 63 nested subqueries. Java has no such bounds and answers. Accepted only for a 400 naming one of those four limits or "recursion limit exceeded" against a Java answer (a sync 200 or an accepted async submit). HPDS_MAX_CROSS_COUNT_ENTRIES, which refuses a valid cross count for the size of its answer rather than the shape of the query, is not covered and stays a reported difference.

rules.name: search-shape-main
rules.reason: Contract, main branch only (javaBranch): Rust serves the consent branch's /search shape, SummaryColumnMeta (name, widthInBytes, categorical, categoryValues, min, max, patientCount, timestampMin, timestampMax, nulls written). The original Java HPDS on main serves ColumnMeta (name, categorical, categoryValues for categorical concepts, min and max for numeric ones, observationCount, patientCount). Accepted only when the bodies are equal once every column meta keeps the shared fields (name, categorical, a non-empty categoryValues, a non-null min and max, patientCount) and, as the main loader also starts max at Double.MIN_VALUE (LoadingStore.java:54), a max of 4.9E-324 against a real max of zero or below takes the real value.

rules.name: authorization-filters-main
rules.reason: Contract, main branch only (javaBranch): Rust, like the consent branch, never applies authorizationFilters (the consent branch only validates them, QueryValidator.java:49), while the original Java HPDS on main ANDs each one into the query (PhenotypicQueryExecutor.java:35), so main answers fewer patients. Rust must not replace a main-branch HPDS that relies on authorizationFilters (README, Differences from Java). Accepted only against main, only when the entry's query carries a non-empty authorizationFilters list, both sides answered (sync 200, or async SUCCESS), and main's answer is the narrower one: a COUNT no greater than Rust's, a cross count with the same concepts at the top level and every count under them no greater, a PATIENTS or DATAFRAME export with the same header and a subset of Rust's rows. Against the consent branch, which ignores the filters as Rust does, any difference stays reported.

rules.name: number-too-long-status
rules.reason: Jackson error, invalid input: Jackson 2.21 refuses a number token with more than 1,000 digits (StreamReadConstraints.getMaxNumberLength, counting integer, fraction and exponent digits). Java answers 400 with Spring's JSON error body when the token is in the request body, and 500 with an empty body when it is in a query sent as a JSON string (PicSureV3Service.convertIncomingQuery). Rust refuses the same tokens with 400 and Jackson's text, "Number value length (<n>) exceeds the maximum allowed (1000, from `StreamReadConstraints.getMaxNumberLength()`)". Two 400s already compare equal, so the rule accepts only that message against a Java 500.

rules.name: string-bound-refused-status
rules.reason: Jackson error, invalid input: a min or max sent as a JSON string that Jackson 2.21's double coercion refuses as malformed ("1d", "1f", "0x1p3", "1_000", "-NaN", "1.e5") makes the Java query fail in convertIncomingQuery, which answers 500 with an empty body; Rust refuses it with 400 "invalid value: string <text>, expected a number, a numeric string, or null". Accepted only when the entry's query holds such a string bound (checked with hpds_query::jackson_string_double), the Java side's 500 has an empty body, and the 400 names that string. Strings refused only for their length are number-too-long-status. Holds on both Java branches, which answer alike.

rules.name: filter-without-criteria-status
rules.reason: Java error, invalid input: a FILTER with neither values nor a min or max (a blank string bound counts as none, since Jackson coerces it to null) makes PhenotypicQueryExecutor throw (PhenotypicQueryExecutor.java:90), so Java answers /query/sync 200 with an empty body and ends POST /query in ERROR; Rust refuses it with 400 "Either values or one of min/max must be set for a filter on <path>". invalid-request-empty-200 covers hpds-bench's own error entry for this; this rule covers any entry whose query holds such a filter, and only with that exact refusal against Java's empty 200 or async ERROR.

rules.name: null-select-status
rules.reason: Java error, invalid input: a null element of select makes Java fail where it reads select. CROSS_COUNT and OBSERVATION_CROSS_COUNT put each path in a map that refuses a null key (CountV3Processor.java:76 and :101 on the consent branch, :76 on main), so /query/sync answers 200 with an empty body; POST /query fails in QueryValidator, which looks every select path up in the dictionary's TreeMap (QueryValidator.java:53 on main, :54 on the consent branch), and answers 200 with no body. Rust refuses those cases with 400 "select holds null, which Java cannot answer here". COUNT, CATEGORICAL_CROSS_COUNT, CONTINUOUS_CROSS_COUNT and INFO_COLUMN_LISTING never read select, and both services answer them as without the null. Accepted only when the query holds a null select element, Rust's 400 is that exact message, and Java's answer is the empty sync 200 or the bodiless async 200.

rules.name: null-concept-path-status
rules.reason: Java error, invalid input: a phenotypic filter whose conceptPath is null makes Java fail on every route (the executor looks the path up on /query/sync and answers 200 with an empty body; on POST /query QueryValidator's dictionary lookup answers 200 with no body, or for ANY_RECORD_OF the job ends in ERROR), and so does an authorization filter whose conceptPath is null on POST /query (PhenotypicFilterValidator.java:29). Rust refuses them with 400 and exactly "a phenotypic filter's conceptPath is null" or "an authorization filter's conceptPath is null" (a missing conceptPath counts as null, as Jackson reads it). Accepted only when the query holds such a filter, Rust's 400 is one of those messages exactly, and Java's answer is one of those three failures. Under the main consent contract the rule covers phenotypic filters only, and Java's 500 counts as its failure too: a null path in an authorization filter is null-authorization-filter-main-status on both routes.

rules.name: null-filter-value-status
rules.reason: Java error, invalid input: a null among a FILTER's values makes Java's executor fail where it looks the value up in a categorical concept's category map (a TreeMap, PhenoCube.java:43), so Java answers /query/sync 200 with an empty body. Java finds nothing for the null in an unknown or numeric concept and ignores values on REQUIRED and ANY_RECORD_OF, and Rust answers those as Java does; on POST /query both end the job in ERROR. Rust refuses the sync case with 400 and exactly "a phenotypic filter's values hold null". Accepted only when the query holds such a value, with that exact refusal against Java's failure.

rules.name: null-result-type-status
rules.reason: Java error, invalid input: a missing or null expectedResultType reaches a switch on it (PicSureV3Service.java:318 on main, :328 on the consent branch, for /query/sync; QueryV3Service.java:118 for POST /query), which throws, so Java answers 200 with no body on both routes. Rust refuses it with 400 and exactly "the query is not valid: expectedResultType is null". Accepted only for such a query, with that exact refusal against those failures.

rules.name: null-filter-type-status
rules.reason: Java error, invalid input: a phenotypic filter whose phenotypicFilterType is null or missing makes Java fail where it switches on the type (the executor on /query/sync, PhenotypicFilterValidator on POST /query), answering 200 with an empty body or no body. Rust refuses it with 400 "a phenotypic filter's phenotypicFilterType is null". INFO_COLUMN_LISTING, which Java answers without evaluating the clause, gets Java's [] from both. Accepted only when the query holds such a filter, with that exact refusal against those failures.

rules.name: null-clause-status
rules.reason: Java error, invalid input: a null among a subquery's phenotypicClauses makes Java's executor fail, answering /query/sync 200 with an empty body and ending POST /query in ERROR. Rust refuses it with 400 "a phenotypic subquery's phenotypicClauses hold null". Accepted only when the query holds such a null, with that exact refusal against those failures.

rules.name: null-authorization-filter-status
rules.reason: Java error, invalid input: on POST /query a null element of authorizationFilters makes QueryValidator throw (it validates each element), answering 200 with no body, on both branches. Rust refuses the submit with 400 "an authorization filter is null". On /query/sync the consent branch ignores the element and answers, as Rust does; main applies it and fails (null-authorization-filter-main). Accepted only for an async entry whose query holds such an element, with that exact refusal against Java's bodiless 200.

rules.name: duplicate-key-in-string-query
rules.reason: Spec, v4 hardening: a query sent as a JSON string with a key repeated in one object is refused by Rust (400 "the query is not valid: duplicate key \"<key>\" at line <n> column <m>"), because a proxy that rewrote the first copy (userConsents) must not be bypassed by a second; Jackson keeps the last value and Java answers. Accepted only when the string query holds that repeated key, Rust names it in that exact form, and Java answered. Under the main consent contract the named key must not be authorizationFilters, whose last value main keeps (Decision 6).

rules.name: unknown-result-type-status
rules.reason: Jackson error, invalid input: an expectedResultType string that is not a name or ordinal of Java's ResultType makes Jackson refuse the query in convertIncomingQuery, which answers 500 with an empty body. Rust refuses it with 400 and exactly "the query is not valid: invalid value: string \"<value>\", expected one of [...]" listing the 14 names. Accepted only for such a value, that exact message and Java's empty 500.

rules.name: result-type-out-of-range-status
rules.reason: Jackson error, invalid input: an expectedResultType that is a boolean, or an integer outside the ordinals of Java's ResultType (0 to 13), makes Jackson's enum coercion refuse the query in convertIncomingQuery, which answers 500 with an empty body on /query/sync and POST /query. Rust refuses it with 400 and exactly "the query is not valid: invalid value: integer `<n>`, expected one of [...]" or "the query is not valid: invalid type: boolean `<b>`, expected one of [...]" listing the 14 names. Accepted only for such a value, that exact message and Java's empty 500.

rules.name: invalid-uuid-status
rules.reason: Jackson error, invalid input: a picsureId or id string Jackson's UUIDDeserializer refuses (neither the canonical form nor 16 bytes of Base64) makes convertIncomingQuery answer 500 with an empty body. Rust refuses it with 400 and exactly "the query is not valid: \"<value>\" is not a UUID in the canonical 8-4-4-4-12 form or 16 bytes of Base64". Accepted only for such a value, that exact message and Java's empty 500.

rules.name: missing-operator-status
rules.reason: Java error, invalid input: a subquery with no operator reaches the switch in PhenotypicQueryExecutor.getReducer with null, which throws, so Java answers /query/sync 200 with an empty body and ends POST /query in ERROR. Rust refuses it with 400 and exactly "a phenotypic subquery must name an operator (AND or OR)". Accepted only when the query holds such a subquery, with that exact message against those failures.

rules.name: consent-extra-field-status
rules.reason: Jackson error, invalid input: a userConsents object with a field other than value is refused by Jackson on the consent branch (and the main branch knows no userConsents field at all), so convertIncomingQuery answers 500 with an empty body. Rust refuses it with 400 and exactly "the query is not valid: unknown field `<name>`, expected `value`". Accepted only when a consent holds such a field, Rust names one of them in that exact form, and Java answered an empty 500.

rules.name: export-type-out-of-scope
rules.reason: Spec, scope: DATAFRAME_TIMESERIES and DATAFRAME_PFB are export types v4 does not produce; POST /query accepts them and ends the query in ERROR with resultMetadata.error "<type> exports are not supported by this phenotype-only HPDS", where Java produces the export. Accepted only for async entries of those two result types, with the Java side named, Java's query in SUCCESS (or its submit answered 200 with no job, Java failing to start the export) and Rust's in ERROR with exactly that reason.

rules.name: null-authorization-filter-main
rules.reason: Java error, deprecated field: the main branch applies authorizationFilters, and a null element, a null conceptPath or a null value in one makes it fail, answering /query/sync 200 with an empty body and ending POST /query in ERROR. Rust never applies authorizationFilters, as the consent branch does not on /query/sync, and answers the query. Accepted only on main, only when the query holds such a null, and only with Java's failure against Rust's answer.

rules.name: empty-subquery-status
rules.reason: Java error, invalid input: a subquery whose phenotypicClauses is empty makes Java's executor fail, so Java answers /query/sync 200 with an empty body (and ends POST /query in ERROR, as Rust does). Rust refuses the sync request with 400 and exactly "a phenotypic subquery must contain at least one clause". invalid-request-empty-200 covers hpds-bench's own error entry for this; this rule covers any entry whose query holds such a subquery, with that exact refusal against Java's empty 200.

rules.name: genomic-no-store-refused
rules.reason: spec-v5-genomic.md section 7, divergences by design: Java with no genomic data (the no-op genomic processor) fails on genomicFilters and answers /query/sync 200 with an empty body or ends POST /query in ERROR; Rust refuses with 400 "genomicFilters is not supported: this HPDS serves no genomic store". Accepted only for that exact message against Java's failure.

rules.name: genomic-null-refused
rules.reason: spec-v5-genomic.md section 7, divergences by design: a genomicFilters entry that is null, a filter whose key is null, or a null inside values makes Java throw a NullPointerException once the genomic step runs (Arrays.sort or binarySearch over the values, zygosity.equals, VariantUtils on a null key); the sync route answers 200 with an empty body and an async query ends in ERROR. Rust answers 400 naming the null. Accepted only when the request's genomic filters hold such a null, Rust's message is its null refusal, and Java failed.

rules.name: genomic-range-refused
rules.reason: spec-v5-genomic.md section 7, divergences by design: a numeric genomic filter with only one of min and max (Range.closed throws a NullPointerException), with min above max by Float.compare (Range.closed throws IllegalArgumentException), or on a column some node holds as categorical (continuousValueIndex is null) makes Java fail; Rust answers 400. Accepted only for those refusals against Java's failure.

rules.name: genomic-spec-key-refused
rules.reason: spec-v5-genomic.md section 7, divergences by design: a spec key matching VariantUtils' patterns whose position is not a Java int (an rs key, a decimal or out of range position) throws in VariantStore.getMasksForDbSnpSpec; Java fails, Rust answers 400 naming the key.

rules.name: genomic-short-spec-refused
rules.reason: v5-genomic-format.md, specs Java cannot parse: when a selected variant's spec has fewer than six fields, new VariantSpec throws in the bucket grouping or the excerpt's TreeMap; Java fails and Rust answers 400.

rules.name: genomic-duplicate-metadata-refused
rules.reason: spec-v5-genomic.md section 7, divergences by design: a variant whose metadata array holds one string twice makes Set.of throw in VariantMetadataIndex.findBySingleVariantSpec, so Java fails the excerpt; Rust answers 400.

rules.name: excerpt-masks-missing-refused
rules.reason: v5-genomic-format.md, excerpts per variant: in local and localDistributed modes a listed variant no node holds masks for makes Optional.get() throw; Java fails the excerpt, Rust answers 400.

rules.name: info-key-delimiter-refused
rules.reason: v5-genomic-format.md, "_____": VariantIndexCache looks a selected key up through (column + "_____" + key).split("_____"); a key or column that does not split back into itself either throws or silently reads another key's variants. Rust refuses with 400; Java's answer is then unchecked.

rules.name: id-cube-numeric-refused
rules.reason: v5-genomic-format.md, ID_CUBE_NAME: when ID_CUBE_NAME names a numeric concept, Java's VCF_EXCERPT casts its values to String for the patient column headers and throws ClassCastException, answering 200 with an empty body; Rust answers 400 naming the setting. Accepted only for VCF_EXCERPT.

rules.name: invalid-genomic-filter-not-evaluated
rules.reason: spec-v5-genomic.md section 7, divergences by design: Rust decides a genomic filter's validity from the request alone, so it refuses an invalid genomic filter even where Java never evaluates it and answers: an empty phenotype cohort (QueryExecutor skips the genomic step and answers 0 or an empty export) or a variant result type with no INFO filter (the variant list skips spec filters and answers empty). Accepted only when Rust's 400 is one of its refusals of a genomic filter and Java's answer is the answer over no patients or no variants.

rules.name: search-values-refused
rules.reason: Spec section 1, /search/values: page or size below 1 (IllegalArgumentException), a page whose (page - 1) * size overflows Java int (subList throws), a missing or non-integer parameter, an unknown column or a column missing on some node (NullPointerException in getInfoStoreValues) make Java answer 500 or 200 with an empty body; Rust answers 400.

rules.name: search-info-column-missing-refused
rules.reason: v5-genomic-format.md, /search refusal: when a search term matches a categorical info column that some node lacks, Java's searchInfoConceptValues dereferences a null info store and answers 200 with an empty body; Rust answers 400.

rules.name: genomic-result-size-limit
rules.reason: spec-v5-genomic.md section 7, divergences by design: excerpt and variant list size limits. Rust refuses an excerpt or a variant list larger than HPDS_MAX_EXCERPT_BYTES with 400 naming the setting; Java builds the answer in memory.

rules.name: variant-list-order
rules.reason: plan-v5.md decision of 2026-10-19 and spec section 6: Java's variant list follows a skip list on one node below the threshold and HashSet order otherwise and after parent merges, which differs between layouts and runs; Rust lists specs in store order. Equal when the two lists hold the same specs.

rules.name: excerpt-order
rules.reason: Spec section 6: VCF_EXCERPT and AGGREGATE_VCF_EXCERPT INFO header columns follow a Java HashSet (ColumnSorter keeps the set's order), each INFO cell joins a HashSet with ',', and the patient-merging parent concatenates groups' patient columns in File.listFiles order. Equal when the INFO columns match as a set, each INFO cell as a multiset of its values, the patient columns as a multiset of (header, column), and every other cell exactly.

rules.name: info-column-listing-order
rules.reason: Spec section 6: INFO_COLUMN_LISTING concatenates node or group lists collected in parallel, so its order is unspecified. Equal as a multiset of entries, min and max compared as floats.

rules.name: search-info-values-order
rules.reason: Spec section 6: the values of /search's info block come from a HashSet built by a parallel collector; compared as sets.

rules.name: search-info-values-and-category-values-order
rules.reason: Spec section 6 together with the v4 rule search-category-values-order: a /search answer whose info values and categoryValues both follow Java hash orders. Equal once both are sorted.

rules.name: search-concept-info-and-category-values-order
rules.reason: Spec section 6 with the v4 rule search-concept-and-category-values-order: the null-term /search answer lists concepts in an unspecified order with categoryValues in hash order, and its info block's values come from a HashSet. Equal once the concept array is sorted by path, every categoryValues array and every info values array sorted.

rules.name: search-values-bucket-order
rules.reason: Spec section 6: /search/values pages follow Java's HashSet order, which Rust reproduces; within one hash bucket the parents' parallel collection leaves the order unspecified. Equal when page and total match and both pages split into the same runs of hash buckets, in the same order and of the same sizes, where every run but the first and the last holds the same values and the first and last runs, which a page boundary may cut out of a larger bucket, may hold other values of that bucket.
